issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אֲרֻחַת יָרָק' means 'a meal of vegetables' (or 'a dish of herbs'), not '青草的飲食' (grass/vegetation food). 'יָרָק' is vegetables/herbs, not grass. Also 'מִשּׁוֹר אָבוּס' means 'than a fatted ox' (a stall-fed ox), not '有牛' (having an ox). The Chinese rendering loses the specific contrast between a simple vegetable meal and a fatted ox, and adds '有' (having) which is not in the Hebrew.
